reviews.title: Toxic cancel process
reviews.text: Cancelling is called “Unsubscribe” which folks might gloss over as “Unsubscribe” is generally attributed to mailing lists. It also required clicking through 5 different screens all with the cancel button on the very bottom with the “keep” button highlighted in bold and very visible. Says a lot about a company when they make a conscious choice to purposely try and deceive users by forcing complicated cancellation methods in an effort to hope folks make mistakes during the process. Better is click cancel -> are you sure yes/no -> if yes, cancel the subscription. Their subscription is also managed outside of the App Store so be mindful of that too. If you rely on managing your subscriptions through the App Store, you’ll never see this subscription in there. These kinds of apps are a dime a dozen so I’ll go with a most honest one.

reviews.title: I use it everyday
reviews.text:
I use Endel every single night to sleep and genuinely don’t want to be without it. It quiets my brain without giving me something else to actively listen to or think about.

I also use it when I’m overstimulated or my brain has way too many tabs open. If my house is loud and chaotic, I’ll put on my headphones and use Endel to drown out the noise and give my brain a chance to reset. I’m literally using it right now while my kids are playing games and yelling in the background. 😂

The focus soundscapes are great when I need to actually get something done, too. It’s become much more than a sleep app for me—it’s something I use throughout the day depending on what my brain needs: sleep, focus, or just a little less noise.

One of the few apps I use every single day and absolutely worth it.

reviews.title: Dishonest company that’s just going to get your money anyway they can
reviews.text: So I did the free trial and realized it just wasn’t something I would really use that much, and didn’t notice any changes while using. So I go to settings and unsubscribe… or so I thought I did. It’s a 5 step process that I thought was just a simple click of a continue button. They first ask if you’ll take a survey before unsubscribing, but you also have the “continue” option. I hit that thinking that was all I needed to do, and I’m sure I was holding my newborn baby or something - because I didn’t notice that there’s actually another question/continue button you have to click. And then there’s another. THEN you are successfully unsubscribed. Well, I didn’t see all these steps until I saw the charge to my bank and went to do a sanity check - so I got charged a full year of an app I didn’t like. So they got me, and I just don’t like businesses that do “gotcha” stuff like that. Don’t trust it and I don’t recommend giving them your support.

reviews.title: Helps me focus
reviews.text:
I’ve had Endel well over a year now. The deep work audio is what I use the most even though I’d really figured it wouldn’t make a difference. 

First, I am a harsh critic because Endel had a lot of ads out on Facebook that made people believe they already had certain sound available (I can’t remember which it was, but was a certain wavelength or biphasic or something) when they actually didn’t, but were only working on bringing it to the app.  I take real issue with that as it roped people into their app under false pretenses, including myself.  I think Endel is a quality product and they can get users with truth and fact just fine and should do so. That being said, I do hope that they eventually are able to bring that audio to the app that they were advertising.

So why do I still give 5 stars?

I have ADHD and the first time I used “deep work” I said it for 50 minutes and before I knew it, the music was stopping. I was focused for that whole 50 minutes and chugged out a bunch of work… It was crazy. I thought it was coincidence so after a break, I did it for another 50 minutes and the same thing happened… I didn’t jump around tabs, I didn’t grab my phone, I just worked for almost an hour straight and that never happens.  I forgot about it the next day and I think it was a couple of days before I used it again and I said it for an hour and a half and again I just worked and was focused the whole time. I forget that Endel is even playing. And I’m just able to stay focused on the task at hand… I don’t know why it helps me so much and maybe it doesn’t help everyone in the same way, but for me, it makes a world of difference. I just wish I remembered to use it more often lol 😂 

I’ve used a few of the relax audios with my daughter and son and it’s been hit or miss. My husband doesn’t care so much for the vibe of the audio (for lack of a better word), but he’s only heard the ones I’ve played and there’s many more to choose from. I like that I can alter the speed and busyness of the audio as well because if it was just sent in Stone, I think I wouldn’t like a lot of of them. Overall, I highly recommend giving it a try even if you don’t struggle with ADHD :)

reviews.title: SCAM APP
reviews.text:
So I want to update my review. I posted earlier and Endel so condescendingly responded they subscription had not been canceled. That’s a whole bunch of garbage try googling: Endel app Reddit and you will see many like me who cancelled and were still charged. 

The first time I cancelled my subscription was 31 hours before the free trial ended. How do I know? I set an alarm to remind me to do it. And then I closed the app out and then went back into it to make sure it had been cancelled and it said it was. The next day I was charged. I am still livid. This is predatory behavior that preys upon people with ADHD and executive dysfunction. I can do everything with spite that strengthens me. 

So, the “second” time I cancelled, I was prompted to verify my email. That’s bizarre, I was never prompted for this before. So I did and then cancelled and wrote my initial one star review. Endel responded saying I never cancelled my subscription. No, and they’re getting reported anywhere and everywhere I can think of. Local news? Board of commissioners meetings? I know they don’t care but they will hear about it, and it will be in meeting notes. State legislators, US representatives and congresspersons will hear about this too. I want everyone to know this is a scam and I don’t want other people falling victim to it. 

It was a glaring red flag to me that this was a scam after I signed up for the free trial. Why? Because the trial didn’t go through the apple App Store and I didn’t realize it until I went to cancel the first of many times.

reviews.text:
The process of canceling is specifically designed to make it difficult. 
Incredibly scam-y. 
Apple should investigate them it’s so bad. 
The process for cancelling purposefully makes you go to different sites, switches yes/no questions, colors asks over and over if you want to stay (sometime asks if you want to cancel) forces you to leave the site then come back to cancel. It’s unethical and gross. Shame on you.

Have reported to our credit card company and Apple.

reviews.title: Unimpressed
reviews.text:
I was pretty unimpressed with the Endel app. I initially downloaded it after seeing an ad on social media promoting their 8D sounds and rhythms, which was the main reason I decided to pay for a subscription. Unfortunately, after subscribing, I found that there was only one 8D sound available. There really isn’t much variety to choose from, and I also feel like the Focus, Sleep, and Relaxation options all sound very similar.
What made the experience even more disappointing is that, despite purchasing a yearly subscription, every time I open the app I’m bombarded with promotions asking me to purchase a lifetime subscription. It’s frustrating to pay for a full year and still constantly feel like I’m being advertised to and pushed to spend more money.
Overall, the app just wasn’t what I expected based on the advertising. I was hoping for a much wider selection of immersive sounds and more variety between the different modes. For the price, I expected a lot more.

reviews.title: Scam & Fraud
reviews.text:
Like hundreds of other reviews here I was scammed by this app. It advertises a free trial but instead charges you for a whole year. The devs will respond to the review and say email us so we can help you but when you email them they reply and say there’s nothing they can do because it’s up to Apple. When you try to refund through Apple for the scam it gets rejected. Somehow Apple unknowingly are helping them scam iOS users and even labeling them as “Editors Choice”, but if you look at all the most recent reviews they are all complaining about this scam.

Edit: Case in point look at the response below by the developer. 
Then I proceeded to email them AGAIN. They told me there’s nothing they can do and directed me back to Apple. This is daylight robbery.

reviews.title: Ads, even though I’ve paid!
reviews.text:
I want to love this app and recommend it to everyone, but I can’t.

I pay for Premium, yet every time I open the app I’m greeted with a full-screen ad that blocks me from doing anything until I close it. I’ve contacted support about it, but nothing has changed.

Why pay for Premium if the experience is still dominated by ads? A weekly promotion or even a banner ad would be much less intrusive (and there are already banner ads).

I’m leaving this review in the hope that someone on the team sees it. I’d switch to another app today if I could find one that didn’t bombard paying customers with full-screen ads.

reviews.title: Premium still has ads
reviews.text:
I do not recommend paying for this app because if you get a subscription they still spam you with full-screen ads for “lifetime” membership each time you open the app. The free functionality is capped at ~10 minute focus sessions. The concept is interesting and helpful for focus, but the full screen ad completely ruins the focus experience, as someone with ADHD that ad is an unacceptable paper-cut and I regret buying the year of “premium.” 

Besides the full-screen ad, there is ALWAYS an ad for lifetime or merch at the top 1/3 of the home page. The developers are so obsessed with a money grab they couldn’t imagine removing the ads even if you pay.

You are not showing your best deals, you are doing fraud by still showing ads when you advertise that premium eliminates ads. False advertising and fraud.

reviews.title: Not for me but I didn’t get a choice
reviews.text: I saw the ads like everyone else. I decided to do the trial. I did not enjoy the user interface. I found it too busy and too complicated, and yet the offerings too simple. I couldn’t find what they were advertising. I have other apps with focus and sleep sounds, that are cheaper. I tried a couple of different things to see if it had some value to me but I decided to end the trial. Except I couldn’t find a way to do that and I was charged for a year subscription. It seems like a predatory practice to lure you in with something in an ad, not deliver, and then make it difficult to cancel the trial. So far no response from the developer.

reviews.title: Ruined by constant upselling to existing premium users
reviews.text:
Endel’s soundscapes are excellent, and I happily pay for Premium. It’s one of my favorite apps for focus and sleep.

Unfortunately, the constant upselling has become a major distraction. Every time I open the app, I’m greeted with a full-screen advertisement for the Lifetime plan. The close button is small and difficult to tap, making it feel like I’m being nudged toward the purchase rather than simply dismissing the promotion.

This is especially disappointing because Endel is designed to reduce stress and distractions. As a paying Premium subscriber, I shouldn’t have to close a full-screen ad every time I launch the app.

If Premium users could permanently dismiss promotional content, I’d happily change this back to 5 stars.
